newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 5.6 pct in Dec.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 5.6 pct in Dec.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate dropped to 5.6 percent in December, from 6.2 percent in November, the state Employment Security Commission said Friday.
That was up from 5.3 percent a year ago.

Retailers hired an additional 2,500 workers to handle the holiday shopping season and while transportation and public utilities added 200 jobs, agency Director Joel Cassidy said. Manufacturing dipped by 200 jobs.

"As our state continues to diversify its labor market and the tourism industry maintains its strong presence, the employment situation in South Carolina should be positive in the coming year," Cassidy said.
Greenville had the state's lowest unemployment rate for December, 2.9 percent, and Williamsburg had the highest, 18.4 percent.
